title: Best SD resources ranked (courses / books / playlists)
relevance: High — meta module for every campus + off-campus HLD/LLD prep path; pick 1–2 primaries, don’t collect 10 courses.
company_notes: Campus/product-cos and some FAANG new-grad: light HLD or TinyURL-style; free stack often enough. Off-campus SDE-1/2 and experienced hire: full HLD with Vol.1 or Grokking plus Hello Interview; Vol.2/DDIA for deeper probing. Indian product cos (Atlassian, Uber, Flipkart): HLD and LLD/machine coding. Meta choice once at prep start; revisit only when a mock exposes a gap.

phases.goal: Establish each resource’s role and a free-first learning sequence for placements prep.

must_hit.point: primer (donnemartin) is the best free syllabus/map: building blocks, performance numbers, Anki decks, sample HLD/OOD — skim outline, return per topic.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names system-design-primer as the map/glossary, not a cover-to-cover read that replaces designing.

must_hit.point: Hello Interview (In a Hurry + How to Prepare + Delivery Framework) is the best free modern guide built from what FAANG interviewers score, including the 45-min skeleton.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says Hello Interview teaches how to run the interview and reuses the delivery skeleton on every design X.

must_hit.point: Gaurav Sen playlist is best free video intuition for scale, microservices, LB, cache, DB tradeoffs; Vol.1 (Alex Xu) is best interview playbook for canonical HLD with 4-step framework and ~16 classic designs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates spoken intuition (Gaurav Sen) from structured canonical designs (Vol.1 / ByteByteGo).

must_hit.point: Role map: primer=glossary/map; Hello Interview=how to run 45 min; Gaurav Sen=spoken intuition; Vol.1/Grokking=practice designs; Vol.2=harder designs; DDIA=why tradeoffs; InterviewReady=paid HLD+LLD depth.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Can assign one job per resource without treating DDIA as an interview script.

probes: Rank the free primaries you’d open first for placements and what job each one does.
What is DDIA for in this stack, and what is it not?

hints.1: Think map vs framework vs video intuition vs practice book.
hints.2: Assign: primer, Hello Interview, Gaurav Sen, Vol.1/Grokking, Vol.2, DDIA, InterviewReady.
hints.3: primer=map; Hello Interview=45-min delivery; Gaurav Sen=intuition; Vol.1/Grokking=designs; Vol.2=harder; DDIA=tradeoff depth not script.

phases.goal: Show how to assemble a stack and run prep with one delivery framework and timed practice.

must_hit.point: Suggested placements stack (~4–8 weeks): primer map → Hello Interview framework → Gaurav Sen playlist → Vol.1 (or Grokking) for 10–15 designs → Vol.2/DDIA chapters only where depth is probed.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the sequence in order and prefers free first before paid deepeners.

must_hit.point: One delivery framework: requirements → estimation → API → data model → high-level diagram → 2–3 deep dives → bottlenecks; Hello Interview and Alex Xu 4-step are the same idea.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks the skeleton without inventing extra steps or treating the two frameworks as conflicting.

must_hit.point: Canonical set is ~15–20 designs (URL shortener, rate limiter, chat, news feed, video, drive, etc.) via Vol.1/Grokking/hq*; LLD is a separate track (OOP/SOLID, patterns, concurrency, parking lot/Splitwise/elevator) via l*/lq* — Vol.1 won’t teach machine coding.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps HLD playbooks and LLD machine-coding resources as separate tracks.

must_hit.point: Self-test: pick a 3-resource stack for 4-week campus prep (one map, one framework, one practice source); timebox one design 45 min on Hello Interview Delivery Framework only; map five hq* to Vol.1 or Grokking or Hello Interview breakdowns.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes drills that force selection, timed delivery, and knowing where to practice each problem.

probes: Build a 3-resource stack for a 4-week campus prep and justify dropping the rest.
Walk the delivery skeleton you’d reuse on every design X.

hints.1: You need one map, one framework, one practice source.
hints.2: Use the ~4–8 week order: primer → Hello Interview → Gaurav Sen → Vol.1 or Grokking.
hints.3: Framework steps: requirements, estimation, API, data model, diagram, 2–3 deep dives, bottlenecks.

phases.goal: Judge buy vs free, practice vs consumption, and when to open depth resources.

must_hit.point: Free path (primer + Hello Interview + Gaurav Sen + ByteByteGo YT) is enough for many campus rounds; pay for Vol.1/Grokking/InterviewReady when you need structured solutions or mocks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Buys only to close a clear gap, not by default prestige.

must_hit.point: Anti-pattern: finishing DDIA or 3 paid courses before ever whiteboard-timing a design — practice > consumption.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Prioritizes timed designs over finishing books/courses first.

must_hit.point: Depth on demand: open DDIA/Vol.2 when follow-ups (quorum, partitioning, exactly-once, geo) keep failing — not as week-1 reading; HLD bar is LB/cache/DB/sharding/queues/consistency/estimation, not implementing Raft/Paxos.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses DDIA/Vol.2 selectively and rejects research-consensus as the interview bar.

must_hit.point: Use one Grokking path (DesignGurus or Educative), not both; coding-parrot dumps are bookmarks after cores, not primary curriculum.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Avoids overlapping paid Grokking tracks and link-dump-as-curriculum.

probes: Given ₹0 vs a book+course budget, what stays free and what do you buy first?
When would you open DDIA or Vol.2 versus staying on Vol.1 practice?

hints.1: Prefer free until a gap is clear.
hints.2: Campus often free stack; buy Vol.1/Grokking/InterviewReady for structured solutions or mocks.
hints.3: Don’t finish DDIA or 3 paid courses before timed whiteboards; open depth when specific follow-ups fail.

phases.goal: Apply stack choice to company settings and fix common prep failure modes.

must_hit.point: Campus/product-cos light HLD: free stack (primer + Hello Interview + Gaurav Sen + a few Vol.1 chapters) usually enough; off-campus/experienced: Vol.1 or Grokking practice set + Hello Interview expected.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Matches stack weight to campus vs full HLD round expectations.

must_hit.point: Indian product cos (Atlassian, Uber, Flipkart): often HLD and LLD/machine coding — don’t stop at Alex Xu alone; add l01+lq*, InterviewReady LLD, or coding-parrot/Low-Level-Design before those rounds.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly adds an LLD resource when the stack is HLD-only.

must_hit.point: Budget/application drill: rewrite stack for ₹0 vs book+course budget; DDIA triage names chapters to skim for chat/news feed/distributed cache and the interview phrases they unlock.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Can rewrite the stack by budget and map selective DDIA chapters to interview language.

probes: You’re interviewing at Flipkart with HLD and machine coding — what do you add to an Alex Xu-only stack?
Someone watched 40 hours of SD YouTube and still freezes — what is missing?

hints.1: Check whether the company asks LLD/machine coding too.
hints.2: Freezing usually means no timed delivery framework and no solo whiteboard reps.
hints.3: Add an LLD track for Atlassian/Uber/Flipkart; fix YouTube-only prep with Hello Interview framework + timed 45-min designs.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Free path (primer + Hello Interview + Gaurav Sen + ByteByteGo YT) covers many campus rounds; buy Vol.1, Grokking, or InterviewReady only when you need structured solutions, mocks, or a combined HLD+LLD video package.

tradeoffs.topic: Practice designs vs consuming DDIA/paid courses
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Practice beats consumption: do not finish DDIA or 3 paid courses before whiteboard-timing designs; open DDIA/Vol.2 only when depth follow-ups keep failing.

tradeoffs.topic: DesignGurus Grokking vs Educative Grokking Modern
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Overlapping walkthroughs of the classic set — pick one Grokking path, not both.

tradeoffs.topic: Vol.1 playbook vs DDIA depth book
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Vol.1/Grokking train canonical interview designs; DDIA builds tradeoff vocabulary (replication, partitioning, transactions, streams) via selective chapters, not as an interview script or week-1 read.
Vol.1 does not teach machine coding; LLD needs a separate track (sheet l*/lq*, InterviewReady LLD, or coding-parrot/Low-Level-Design), especially for Indian product cos.

gotchas.trap: Watched 40 hours of SD YouTube but freezes in the room
gotchas.correction: Missing a timed delivery framework plus solo whiteboard reps — use Hello Interview Delivery Framework and timebox 45-min designs.

gotchas.trap: Buying both DesignGurus Grokking and Educative Grokking Modern
gotchas.correction: They overlap; use one Grokking path only.

gotchas.trap: Reading all of DDIA before any design practice
gotchas.correction: Classic stall — interviewers reward applied tradeoffs, not chapter recall; practice first, skim selective chapters on demand.

gotchas.trap: Treating Vol.1 diagrams as the only correct architecture
gotchas.correction: Interviewers poke alternatives; defend tradeoffs rather than recite one diagram.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring LLD until the night before an Atlassian/Flipkart machine-coding round
gotchas.correction: LLD is a separate skill from HLD playbooks — add an LLD resource earlier.

gotchas.trap: Chasing every newsletter/video instead of finishing designs end-to-end
gotchas.correction: Finish ~15 designs with estimation and one deep dive each rather than collecting more content.
